data.title: Command-Line Parser
data.solution:
from re import search as S,sub
C=open(0).read()
V="[aeiouAEIOU]"*("-y"in C)
i=S("-t\w* (\w+)",C)
j=S("-k\w*( \w+)+",C)
T=sub(V,"",i.group(1))if i else""
K=[sub(V,"",k)for k in j.group().split()[1:]]if j else[]
print(" ".join([f"[{k}]"for k in K if k]+([T]if T else []))or"<BLANK>")
data.statement:
A (fictional) terminal command called {{cdgm}} has the following command-line arguments:

• {{-y}} / {{--yes}}: takes no values.
• {{-t}} [[title]] / {{--title}} [[title]]: specifies a [[title]] value.
• {{--keyword}} [[keyword1]] [[keyword2]] ... [[keywordN]]: specifies [[N]] space-separated [[keyword]] value(s).

These arguments appear <<at most once>> in <<any order>> after the {{cdgm}} command, separated by singular spaces. Their corresponding values follow the order in which these arguments appear. Based on the given command line,

• If any [[keyword]] is/are specified, print them in-order as "{{[}}[[keyword]]{{]}}" separated by singular spaces.
• If a [[title]] is specified, print it after all printed [[keyword]](s), separated by a singular space.
• If {{-y}}/{{--yes}} is specified, remove all vowels ({{a}}, {{e}}, {{i}}, {{o}}, {{u}}, case-insensitive) from every [[keyword]] and/or [[title]] before printing. If the [[keyword]] and/or [[title]] only contains vowels, <<do not print it>>.
• Lastly, strip all leading and trailing whitespace. If there is nothing to print, output {{<BLANK>}} instead.

<<Examples>>
```>> cdgm
<BLANK>

>> cdgm --keyword a b Cdefg --title Spell
[a] [b] [Cdefg] Spell

>> cdgm --yes --title Spell --keyword A B CdEfg
[B] [Cdfg] Spll```

• It will only contain at most one {{-y}}/{{--yes}} argument, at most one {{-t}}/{{--title}} argument, and at most one {{--keyword}} argument. It will not contain any other argument.
• Values (non-arguments) in the command line will only appear directly after its corresponding {{-t}}/{{--title}} or {{--keyword}} arguments.

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

A (fictional) terminal command called cdgm has the following command-line arguments:

• -y / --yes: takes no values.
• -t title / --title title: specifies a title value.
• --keyword keyword1 keyword2 ... keywordN: specifies N space-separated keyword value(s).

These arguments appear at most once in any order after the cdgm command, separated by singular spaces. Their corresponding values follow the order in which these arguments appear. Based on the given command line,

• If any keyword is/are specified, print them in-order as "[keyword]" separated by singular spaces.
• If a title is specified, print it after all printed keyword(s), separated by a singular space.
• If -y/--yes is specified, remove all vowels (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive) from every keyword and/or title before printing. If the keyword and/or title only contains vowels, do not print it.
• Lastly, strip all leading and trailing whitespace. If there is nothing to print, output <BLANK> instead.

Examples
>> cdgm
<BLANK>

>> cdgm --keyword a b Cdefg --title Spell
[a] [b] [Cdefg] Spell

>> cdgm --yes --title Spell --keyword A B CdEfg
[B] [Cdfg] Spll





   

      
Input

      
Line 1: A positive integer L; the length of the command line.
Line 2: A L-character string; the command line.

   

   

      
Output

      
Line 1: The required output as per the given command line.

   

   

      
Constraints

      
4 ≤ L ≤ 60
1 ≤ N ≤ 5
Each title and/or keyword is non-empty and only contains English letter(s).
The given command line will always be valid:
• It will always start with cdgm.
• It will only contain at most one -y/--yes argument, at most one -t/--title argument, and at most one --keyword argument. It will not contain any other argument.
• Values (non-arguments) in the command line will only appear directly after its corresponding -t/--title or --keyword arguments.
• Values in the command line will always follow the specified command-line syntax (singular spacing, expected number of values, etc.).

   

   

      
Example

      

         

            
Input

            
18
cdgm --title Hello

         

         

            
Output

            
Hello
